tldr: Moonshot AI retired Kimi K2.5 for the 2.8-trillion-parameter K3 in late August, drawing early hands-on tests inside Claude Code. Days later, Reuters reported the startup was courting US cloud giants to host K3, setting up a bigger commercial push.
whats_new: Moonshot confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO on Sept 3 — six outlets report a target valuation as high as $50 billion and a listing as early as Q4.
why_it_matters: A Hong Kong listing is a concrete signal on Moonshot's long-term viability before you deepen a K3 integration, and the reported US-cloud hosting talks could change where and how you deploy it.

status.detail: Moonshot confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO targeting up to $50B, as early as Q4, while K3 remains its flagship model amid reported talks to host it on US clouds.

beats.headline: Kimi K3 (2.8T params) replaces K2.5 as Moonshot's flagship, put through hands-on tests inside Claude Code
Reuters: Moonshot in talks with US cloud giants to host K3
Moonshot confidentially files for a Hong Kong IPO targeting up to $50B
beats.summary: Six independently bylined outlets report the same confidential filing the same day, with target figures ranging from a $3B raise to a $50B valuation and a possible Q4 listing.

open_questions: Which US cloud provider(s), if any, will end up hosting Kimi K3?
Does the IPO filing come with any near-term API pricing or support changes for K3?
Is the $50 billion valuation figure Moonshot's own target, or an outside estimate ahead of the listing?
take_for_builders: Track Moonshot's IPO progress for signs of API pricing or support-tier changes before deepening a K3 integration, and watch the reported US-cloud talks for new deployment options.
